newsitem.title: ROMANIA: ROMANIA HUNTS MOSQUITOS BEHIND MENINGITIS EPIDEMIC.
newsitem.headline: ROMANIA HUNTS MOSQUITOS BEHIND MENINGITIS EPIDEMIC.

text.p: Romanian and U.S. medical experts have joined hands to track down a type of mosquito believed to be the carrier of a virus which killed 40 people in Balkan country's worst viral meningitis epidemic in a decade.

"Some 70 local specialists and visiting epidemiologists from the U.S. Center of Disease Control will capture mosquitos and send them to France's Pasteur Institute to see whether they are infected with the virus which caused the (meningitis) epidemic," Adrian Strainu-Cercel, a senior health ministry official, told a news conference on Thursday.
As many as 453 patients, including some 50 children, were hospitalised across Romania after the epidemic erupted at the end of July. Of the 40 death toll, most were elderly people.
Lab tests conducted at the Paris-based Pasteur Institute confirmed that the patients were suffering from the West Nile virus.
"We isolated the virus, now we must identify the carrier, which mosquito species is responsible for spreading the disease," Strainu-Cercel said.
Lack of hygiene is behind meningitis spread. The viral disease, which usually lasts a week, causes high fever, headaches and vomiting and affects the gastro-intestinal tract.
There is no specific drug treatment for the virus, which can degenerate into a fatal inflammation of the brain, known as meningoencephalitis.
In 1986 Romania suffered an epidemic of the more dangerous bacterial meningitis which killed some 15,000 people in central Africa this year.
